key_insight: PanDent shows that dental MLLMs can sound fluent while still missing tooth-level clinical accuracy, and that expert-grounded fine-tuning improves structure-language consistency.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark helps assess whether AI-generated panoramic radiology reports align with dentist-validated findings, which is important for reliable dental decision support.
method: Built a large OPG benchmark with 9,524 high-quality panoramic radiographs.
Created fine-grained tooth-level annotations by experienced dentists and validated them by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist.
Converted expert findings into clinically consistent reports using defined reporting logic for structure-to-text evaluation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across proprietary, open-source, and medical-specific MLLMs, showing fluent outputs but substantial tooth-level localization and diagnosis errors, with clear gains after PanDent fine-tuning.
watch_item: Because PanDent is built from expert-validated annotations and reporting rules, performance gains may not fully generalize to noisier real-world clinical workflows or different imaging settings.
paper_title: PanDent: Toward Comprehensive Tooth-Level Structure-Language Consistency in Dental Radiology
